This feature is available in AWS Regions where both Global Resolver and AWS Cloud WAN are available. To learn more about Global Resolver, see the product page . To get started, see Route 53 Global Resolver Developer Guide .

items.title: AWS Workload Credentials Provider adds container support for ACM certificates
items.description: The open source AWS Workload Credentials Provider can now export AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificates to applications running in containers on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), including AWS Fargate, Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), and Docker on Amazon EC2. You can now automate certificate deployment and renewal for containerized TLS workloads the same way you do on EC2 instances, on both Linux and Windows. The provider runs as a sidecar in your ECS task or EKS pod. It exports each certificate and private key to a shared volume and writes the renewed files when ACM rotates the certificate. For TLS servers that don't reload certificate files on their own, such as NGINX, Apache, HAProxy, or IIS, a companion watcher in the TLS container runs your reload command after each renewal. The watcher needs no AWS credentials. TLS servers that reload automatically, such as Envoy, Traefik, and Caddy, need only the shared volume. Access is controlled through IAM: the sidecar assumes a per-workload role that is allowed to export only that workload's certificates. To get started, download the provider and watcher binaries for Linux (x86_64 and Arm64) or Windows, and follow the setup steps and ECS and EKS examples in the AWS Workload Credentials Provider README on GitHub. The provider is available at no additional charge, and standard ACM charges apply to exported certificates. To learn more, see the AWS Certificate Manager documentation .

items.title: AWS WAF announces simplified onboarding for Bot Control targeted protection
items.description: Today, AWS WAF announces a simplified console experience for Bot Control at the targeted inspection level. A single setting, Targeted bot control, turns on targeted protection for your Amazon CloudFront distributions with the configuration AWS recommends. It comes with two additions to the Bot Control managed rule group: bot confidence levels, which summarize the targeted detections on each request as High, Medium, or Low, and a LATEST version that keeps you on the newest detections automatically. Together, they help you protect your applications against sophisticated and AI-powered bots without writing label match rules or changing application code. The targeted inspection level uses machine learning and client-side signals to detect evasive bots. Previously, acting on those signals meant integrating the AWS WAF JavaScript SDK into every page, learning dozens of labels, and writing label match rules to combine them. Now, the rule group combines the detections into one confidence level per request, with one rule per level, and the Targeted bot control setting adds the rule group, applies the recommended action for each level, sets the version to LATEST, and turns on automatic SDK integration so CloudFront adds the SDK to your pages. You can change any action or start in Count. The Targeted bot control setting is available today for protection packs (web ACLs) used with Amazon CloudFront. Bot confidence levels and the LATEST version are available in all AWS Regions where AWS WAF Bot Control is available. Standard pricing for the targeted inspection level applies, with no additional charge for the setting or automatic SDK integration. To get started, open the AWS WAF console. To learn more, see Turning on Targeted bot control and Bot confidence levels in the AWS WAF Developer Guide, and read the AWS Security Blog post .

items.title: AWS Transit Gateway supports native integration with Gateway Load Balancer
items.description: AWS Transit Gateway now supports network function attachments of type Gateway Load Balancer, simplifying the deployment and management of network security across your AWS network. With a network function attachment, you can connect your transit gateway to a Gateway Load Balancer VPC endpoint service that fronts firewalls and other security appliances without complex VPC configurations. Transit Gateway creates and manages the Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in the Availability Zones you choose, removing the need to create dedicated endpoint subnets and route tables. The endpoint service can be in another AWS account. Network function attachments also support context sharing with security services. Transit Gateway adds resource context to traffic sent to your firewall, including the transit gateway attachment, VPC, subnet, and security groups. Your firewall can use this context alongside IP addresses to enforce segmentation policies. This capability is available in all commercial AWS Regions where both AWS Transit Gateway and Gateway Load Balancer are available, except Middle East (Bahrain) and Middle East (UAE). It is also available in the AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West) Regions. To get started, see Network function attachments in the AWS Transit Gateway Guide and visit the AWS Transit Gateway product page .

items.title: Amazon S3 Storage Lens now tracks S3 Intelligent-Tiering access tiers
items.description: Amazon S3 Storage Lens now provides storage metrics for each S3 Intelligent-Tiering access tier. You can see object counts and storage bytes in every tier across your buckets. This helps you track how your data moves between tiers, estimate storage costs, and measure your savings. S3 Storage Lens gives you visibility across your organization into storage usage and activity to help you optimize costs and performance. Access tier metrics appear in your S3 Storage Lens dashboards and metrics exports alongside your existing metrics. S3 Storage Lens also now publishes prefix metrics to AWS Billing and Cost Management, so you can allocate shared bucket costs to teams and applications with split cost allocation data for S3. To get started, enable access tier metrics in your S3 Storage Lens advanced tier configuration. Access tier metrics are available in all AWS Regions, except the AWS China Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, visit the S3 Storage Lens documentation . For pricing, visit the S3 pricing page .

items.title: Amazon ECR now replicates image deletions across regions and accounts
items.description: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports replicating image deletions and tag removals to your replication destinations. Previously, ECR replication copied images to destination regions and accounts but did not replicate deletions, requiring you to manage deletions separately in each location. With replication of deletes, your destination repositories stay consistent with the source automatically. Teams running multi-region or multi-account architectures no longer need to script or manually track image cleanup across every destination. When you delete an image or remove a tag in your source registry, whether directly or through a lifecycle policy, ECR propagates that deletion to each destination in the replication rule. Replicated deletions emit EventBridge events and are recorded in CloudTrail, so you have the same visibility into deletions as you do for image pushes. Replication of deletes is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon ECR is available, at no additional cost. To get started, update your replication configuration in the Amazon ECR console or AWS CLI. For more information, see the Amazon ECR User Guide .

items.title: Amazon EBS now supports associating additional KMS keys with snapshots
items.description: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) now supports associating additional AWS Key Management Service (KMS) keys with EBS snapshots. This new capability enables you to share and copy encrypted snapshots across accounts without first re-encrypting them, simplifying your disaster recovery and backup workflows. Customers use EBS snapshots as durable, point-in-time backups of EBS volumes. By associating an additional customer-managed KMS key (CMK) with a snapshot encrypted with an AWS managed key (AMK), for example, you enable cross-account sharing for that snapshot without re-encrypting its data. This feature accelerates your disaster recovery workflows and enhances operational efficiency for enterprise backup administrators and disaster recovery teams. Support for associating additional KMS keys with Amazon EBS snapshots is available in all AWS commercial, China, AWS GovCloud (US), and AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Regions, plus AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts. You can access this capability through the AWS Console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), and AWS SDKs. To learn more, see the Amazon EBS documentation .

items.title: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports hybrid search combining vector and full text for more relevant search results
items.description: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports hybrid search that combines vector similarity search with full-text search within a single query. By combining semantic meaning and exact term matching into a single ranked list of results, hybrid search captures both intent and precise terms for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent memory, and search applications. This can deliver more relevant ranked results than either method alone. Hybrid search works with the same S3 Vectors APIs and maintains subsecond latency for infrequent queries and latency around 100 milliseconds or less for frequent queries. S3 Vectors is designed to provide the same elasticity, durability, and availability as Amazon S3, and it reduces the total costs of storing and querying vectors by up to 90% compared to alternative vector solutions. With hybrid search, customers can now store the data that they want to make full-text searchable alongside the vectors. Customers write data with the PutVectors API as they do today and include the searchable text as another metadata field. S3 Vectors then automatically indexes that field for full-text search with BM25 relevance scoring. By default, S3 Vectors uses a language-agnostic text analyzer to index this data which works across most languages, and customers can optionally select a language-specific analyzer for more accurate language-aware matching. To perform a hybrid query, customers send their query text strings alongside their query vector in a single QueryVectors call; S3 Vectors runs both a vector search and a full-text search, fuses the two with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), and returns a single ranked list of the top K requested results. Customers can also run full-text and vector queries separately to apply own ranking logic, search across multiple text fields in a single query, and enable full-text search on existing data in place. Hybrid search is available today in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon S3 Vectors is available, and in the AWS China Regions. To get started, use the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or the Amazon S3 console. To learn more, visit the Amazon S3 Vectors documentation , and the Amazon S3 pricing page for pricing.

items.title: Amazon Redshift now supports multi-statement transactions, conflict resolution, and time travel for Apache Iceberg
items.description: Amazon Redshift now supports multi-statement transactions, automatic write-conflict resolution, and time travel for Apache Iceberg tables. You can run multi-step, concurrent transformation pipelines directly on Iceberg tables and audit the results, with the transaction semantics you expect from a data warehouse. This helps anyone writing to Iceberg tables at production scale. Batch jobs get all-or-nothing commits across multiple steps. Streaming and scheduled jobs can write to the same tables at the same time. Analysts, auditors, and AI agents can query a table as it existed at any point in time. With multi-statement transactions, you group several statements in a single BEGIN…COMMIT statement and publish them as one atomic Iceberg snapshot. This means a multi-step load such as a MERGE followed by a DELETE, can be commited together as one atomic operation, are never queryable in a half-applied state, and roll back cleanly if there's a failure. Automatic conflict resolution lets concurrent writes, such as streaming inserts alongside scheduled deletes, write to the same table and commit together when their changes don't overlap, instead of failing and retrying. Time travel lets you query a table as it existed at a past point in time with AS OF TIMESTAMP. You can use it to reproduce reports, audit changes, or recover from a bad write without keeping extra copies. These capabilities are available in all AWS commercial Regions for Amazon Redshift’s provisioned RG or serverless clusters that are writing to or querying Iceberg tables.. To get started, see the following list of resources: 1/ Resolving concurrent writes for Apache Iceberg tables using Amazon Redshift 2/ Multi-statement transactions for Apache Iceberg tables in Amazon Redshift 3/ Time travel support for Apache Iceberg

items.title: AWS DevOps Agent is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-West)
items.description: Now available in AWS GovCloud (US-West), AWS DevOps Agent is your always-available operations teammate that resolves and proactively prevents incidents, optimizes application reliability and performance, and handles on-demand SRE tasks across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments. DevOps Agent investigates incidents and identifies operational improvements as an experienced teammate would: by learning your applications and their relationships, working with your observability tools, runbooks, code repositories, and CI/CD pipelines, and correlating telemetry, code, and deployment data. It autonomously triages incidents and guides teams to rapid resolution, reducing mean time to resolution (MTTR) from hours to minutes, while analyzing patterns across historical incidents to deliver actionable recommendations that prevent future outages. For the full list of AWS Regions where AWS DevOps Agent is available, visit the Regions list. Pricing details are available on the AWS DevOps Agent pricing page . AWS Support customers receive monthly DevOps Agent credits based on the prior month's AWS Support charge: 100% for Unified Operations, 75% for Enterprise Support, or 30% for Business Support+. For many customers, this significantly reduces or eliminates DevOps Agent costs. For details, visit the support compare page . To learn more, read the launch blog and see getting started .

items.title: Amazon Connect Health medical coding is now available in public preview
items.description: Today, AWS announces the public preview of medical coding in Amazon Connect Health , a HIPAA-eligible AI service that works alongside healthcare teams across patient engagement and point-of-care workflows. Medical coding uses existing clinical documentation to suggest ICD-10-CM and CPT codes, including E&M levels and modifiers, for a provider or coder to review and approve before submission. You can integrate medical coding into your EHR or billing application through the Amazon Connect Health SDK, or use it with Amazon Connect Health ambient documentation. Each code links to the evidence that supports it and carries a confidence score, so reviewers can confirm a code before a claim goes out. In this public preview, you can choose to upload your organization's previously coded encounters, and the service builds a coding reference set specific to your organization. The corrections coders make feed that reference set and improve future coding suggestions. Medical coding is available in public preview in the US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) AWS Regions. To learn more, see medical coding in the Amazon Connect Health user guide.

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer agent assist now supports interactive responses
items.description: Amazon Connect Customer agent assist now supports interactive components, including cards, carousels, buttons, and input fields. The AI agent analyzes conversation context in real time, recommends actions, retrieves information, and executes tasks on behalf of contact center agents using MCP tools in Connect Customer or third-party services. Interactive responses let agents review information, provide details, select options, and confirm actions without manually typing a separate request for each action. The AI agent can also recommend step-by-step guides, cases, customer profiles, and third-party applications that agents can open with one click. For example, when a customer calls to dispute a charge, the AI agent can dynamically generate an interactive list of the customer’s recent transactions. The agent can select the disputed transaction, provide or confirm the required details, and approve the action. The AI agent can then use a connected tool to create the dispute request and display confirmation in the agent workspace. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Connect Customer agent assist is available. To learn more and get started, see Agent Assist in the Amazon Connect Administrator Guide.

items.title: AWS KMS now supports key sharing with AWS Resource Access Manager
items.description: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now integrates with AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM), giving you a simpler and more consistent way to share KMS keys across your AWS accounts, within your organization in AWS Organizations, and with specific IAM roles and users. You can now let trusted parties define the access they need through reusable managed permissions in RAM, while keeping full control of your keys and key policies. To share a key, create a resource share by selecting the keys to share, choosing a managed permission, and specifying the principals. You can use AWS managed permissions for common scenarios, or customer managed permissions (CMPs) authored by you or by trusted parties such as SaaS providers and central security teams. Sharing KMS keys through RAM makes enabling cross-account access faster to set up and safer to maintain. The trusted parties who need access to your keys can publish the policy once as a CMP, without the need for you to modify the key policies by hand. You simply fill in the values that scope it to your environment and attach it to the resource share. Your existing key policy is untouched, so you are always in control of your key as your environment grows. When a new policy version is available via an updated CMP, you decide when to apply it to your resource shares. This enhancement is built on new AWS RAM capabilities that are available for every resource type RAM supports. CMPs now support multiple policy statements and additional IAM condition operators, including StringNotEquals, BoolIfExists, and ArnLike, along with the ForAnyValue and ForAllValues prefixes, so you can express precise, least-privilege access. The parameterized managed permissions lets you place a temporary placeholder in CMPs that allows each resource share owner to customize and scope down CMPs to their environment, enabling CMPs to be reused and serve many accounts. CMPs can now be published and shared across accounts, so the authors can maintain one permission, manage its versions centrally, and see every resource share that uses it, while other accounts can use it directly without keeping their own copy. KMS key sharing with RAM is available in all AWS Regions where both services are available, except the Middle East (UAE) and Middle East (Bahrain). For more information, see Sharing KMS keys with AWS RAM in the AWS KMS Developer Guide and Working with shared AWS resources in the AWS RAM Developer Guide.

items.title: Set up, connect, and govern AI agents faster with Amazon WorkSpaces
items.description: Building AI agents has become essential. Across your organization, teams want agents to handle ERP transactions, work through a claims queue, and operate the same applications your people use every day. But how do you move from experiments to production? Before an agent touches real systems and real data, you need to verify who it acted on behalf of, what it did, and whether it stayed within the limits you set. Without that visibility, the agent stays stuck in testing, and the value is never realized. Earlier this year, we launched Amazon WorkSpaces for AI agents , extending the power and security of a cloud work environment to agents, not just people. Today, we're excited to announce new capabilities that make it even easier to operate agents confidently across your enterprise and move them from proof of concept to governed production in fewer steps.  You can set up new agents or connect the ones your builders have already built, run them under your own identity providers and policies, and keep a record of everything they do. You don't need to stitch together new tools or build custom monitoring. Setup used to mean configuring the machine by hand. Now, you can just describe what your agent needs to your AI coding assistant such as Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro. Guided by AWS MCP skills, the assistant builds the WorkSpace from defaults you can adjust. If your teams build on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, you can connect an agent directly with your AWS credentials and skip writing any agent code. New tools also reduce agent costs and increase accuracy by letting an agent carry out a series of actions in a single call and use the computer-use actions its model already knows. But an agent that can work is not necessarily an agent you can trust with mission-critical work and sensitive data. This release gives you the same oversight over an agent that you have over the employees you manage. First, agents can now sign in through any identity provider (IdP) that supports OIDC, in addition to the existing SAML support. Administrators can send sign-in straight to their IdP, so users authenticate with their usual corporate credentials, and you don't build custom authentication. Second, with on-behalf-of (OBO) sign-in, an agent works as the signed-in user, with that user's existing directory identity, permissions, and Group Policies on the desktop.  WorkSpaces now offers session replay, giving you a reviewable record of what your agent did. Session replay turns session screenshots into a video and pairs it with a plain-language transcript of the agent's actions. Both are stored in your own Amazon S3 bucket and encrypted with your own keys. Your security team can see what the agent saw, and your compliance team gets evidence to support audits. Together, these updates help move agents out of pilots and into real production scale. Your teams can keep working the way they do today, with agents working alongside them in familiar and trusted cloud work environments. And every one of those agents is held to the same identity, policy, and audit standards as the rest of your workforce. With WorkSpaces, you can bring AI agents into your business without rebuilding decades of software or needing a separate environment to govern them. To get started operating AI agents on WorkSpaces, visit our documentation page .

items.title: AWS Marketplace Metering Service now supports decimal usage quantities
items.description: AWS Marketplace Metering Service now supports decimal usage quantities in the MeterUsage and BatchMeterUsage APIs. Previously, AWS Marketplace sellers reported usage to both APIs in whole numbers, and now they can report usage with up to six decimal places. Sellers can price and meter in the units that match how customers consume their product, for example reporting 1.5 terabytes (TB) of storage instead of 1 or 2 TB. To report decimal quantities, sellers use the new UsageQuantityAsDecimal parameter in MeterUsage and QuantityAsDecimal parameter in BatchMeterUsage, and existing integrations that report whole numbers continue to work without changes. Usage allocations, which split reported usage into buckets by tags, also support decimal quantities with the new AllocatedUsageQuantityAsDecimal parameter. This new feature is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace Metering Service is available. To learn more, see MeterUsage and BatchMeterUsage in the AWS Marketplace API Reference.

items.title: AWS Secrets Manager adds managed external secrets support for Auth0, Okta, and Palo Alto Networks
items.description: AWS Secrets Manager now supports managed external secrets for Auth0, Okta, and Palo Alto Networks. Long-lived credentials that are not rotated increase the risk of unauthorized access if exposed. Rotating a third-party credential requires coordinated updates to the external service and every application that uses it. You set a rotation schedule from the AWS Management Console or API. Secrets Manager rotates the credential and stores the current value without a custom rotation Lambda function. Secrets Manager offers self-rotation and administrator-assisted rotation for Auth0 credentials. With self-rotation, the target application replaces its own secret. With administrator-assisted rotation, a separate Auth0 application with Management API permissions replaces the target application's secret. For Okta, Secrets Manager offers administrator-assisted rotation with a separate administrator JSON Web Token (JWT) key and validates the replacement before deactivating the old secret. For Palo Alto Networks, Secrets Manager offers self-rotation, in which the current API key authorizes its replacement. Applications that already retrieve credentials from Secrets Manager receive the rotated value without a code change or deployment. These integrations join existing managed external secrets support for BigID, Cisco Security Platform, Confluent Cloud, Databricks, Datadog, GitLab, Jenkins, MongoDB Atlas, Netskope, Paddle, Salesforce, Snowflake, SonarQube, and Twilio. Auth0, Okta, and Palo Alto Networks managed external secrets are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Secrets Manager managed external secrets is supported. To learn more, visit the   AWS Secrets Manager managed external secrets documentation  .

items.title: IAM Identity Center now supports VPC endpoints and network access controls
items.description: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports interface VPC endpoints powered by AWS PrivateLink and network access controls, enabling you to keep IAM Identity Center traffic private and restrict which networks can reach your IAM Identity Center services. Previously, IAM Identity Center rejected traffic arriving through VPC endpoints, requiring all sign-in and API traffic to use public endpoints. With this launch, you can create interface VPC endpoints for AWS access portal and service APIs to route traffic over the AWS private network. IAM Identity Center sign-in traffic flows through the AWS Sign-in VPC endpoint. You can attach VPC endpoint policies to each endpoint to scope which AWS organizations, accounts and resources are reachable through your private connection. Network access controls add a second layer of enforcement at the IAM Identity Center instance level. When enabled, you can require that all access arrive through a VPC endpoint, allow specific IP address ranges or VPCs as trusted sources, and exclude individual applications from enforcement to accommodate services that connect from outside your VPC. SCIM provisioning traffic from your external identity provider can be independently restricted to known IP address ranges. Network access controls are configured through the IAM Identity Center API and are disabled by default. This capability is available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions at no additional cost. To learn more, see Interface VPC endpoints in the IAM Identity Center User Guide. For more information, visit the IAM Identity Center product page .

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports KV cache-aware routing for real-time inference endpoints
items.description: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports KV cache-aware routing for real-time inference endpoints, enabling you to reduce time to first token for LLM workloads with long or repeated prompts. Serving engines such as vLLM store the computed key-value (KV) cache for repeated prompt starts such as shared system prompts, documents, and conversation history, to skip repeated work. Across several instances, a request that lands where the cache is missing recomputes it. Under high load, instances also evict cached blocks to free GPU memory, including shared prompts and earlier conversation turns. KV cache-aware routing sends each request to the instance that holds the longest matching part of its prompt in cache. The vLLM container reports the cache blocks it stores and evicts, and SageMaker routes with that live view. If the lookup is slow or finds no match, the endpoint falls back to load-aware routing, so the request is still served. Prefix-aware routing suits stable shared prompts, short prompts, or moderate load. KV cache-aware routing suits long prompts, high load, and limited GPU memory. Customers can now enable this feature by setting `RoutingStrategy` to `KV_AWARE` on a production variant and adding one environment variable so the container reports cache events. Customer can invoke the endpoint with the same APIs and OpenAI-compatible payloads. It supports single-model endpoints and inference components, including LoRA adapters, on GPU instances. It requires the AWS vLLM Deep Learning Container version 0.33.0 or later with at least two instances or inference component copies. Detailed observability metrics show KV cache hit rate. There is no additional charge for KV cache-aware routing. KV cache-aware routing is available today in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker AI is available. To get started, update to the latest AWS SDK or CLI. To learn more, visit the Amazon SageMaker AI inference page and see the API documentation .

items.title: AWS Network Firewall now supports context-aware rules with AWS Transit Gateway-attached firewalls
items.description: AWS Network Firewall attached to AWS Transit Gateway now allows you to use context-aware rules in your firewall policy. Network Firewall is a managed firewall and intrusion prevention service that inspects and filters traffic across your virtual private clouds (VPCs). With context-aware rules, you write rules that reference context from VPC resources instead of IP addresses. This makes it easier to apply consistent security controls as your organization grows. Existing rules automatically cover new workloads, so you don't need to update rules manually. Context-aware rules match traffic using VPCs, subnets, security groups, and Transit Gateway attachment identifiers, collectively known as context identifiers. You can reference context identifiers in a rule's source for any protocol, and in its destination for TCP-based protocols such as HTTP, TLS, and SSH. Flow and alert logs include context identifiers, so you can investigate activity based on context. Context-aware rules are available at no additional charge in all commercial and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. For a full list of supported Regions, see the AWS Capabilities by Region page . To learn more, see the AWS Network Firewall product page and documentation .

items.title: AWS Security Hub now detects when vulnerable software is running on Amazon EC2 instances
items.description: AWS Security Hub now detects when software with a known vulnerability is actively running on your Amazon EC2 instances. Exposure findings now include a new trait, *The EC2 instance is running software with a known vulnerability*. These findings get a higher severity rating than findings for the same vulnerability where the software isn't running. This helps your security team focus on the vulnerabilities that pose the greatest risk, without investing time and resources to investigate if the software is actually in use. Security teams managing thousands of instances can now prioritize patching based on actual runtime risk.  Security Hub correlates data from Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring and Amazon Inspector VM Scanner to detect running vulnerable software. It then combines this with other signals to generate exposure findings for EC2 resources that may be at risk, so you can prioritize response and remediation. This capability is available at no additional cost with the AWS Security Hub Essentials plan in all AWS Regions where Security Hub is available . To learn more, see the AWS Security Hub User Guide , the exposure definition in Remediating exposures for EC2 , the AWS Security Hub product page , the GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring User Guide , and the Amazon Inspector VM Scanner User Guide . For the full list of Regions, see the AWS Regional Services List .

items.title: AWS Backup adds logically air-gapped vault support for Amazon RDS
items.description: AWS Backup logically air-gapped vault now supports Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) DB instances. Logically air-gapped vaults are a type of AWS Backup vault that stores immutable, isolated backups, which are locked by default with AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode. Secure sharing across accounts and AWS Organizations enables direct restore, reducing recovery time from a data loss event. You can now protect your Amazon RDS DB instances in logically air-gapped vaults. A logically air-gapped vault stores immutable backups that are locked by default, and isolated with encryption using AWS owned keys or customer-managed keys. This helps reduce the risk of downtime, ensure business continuity, and meet compliance requirements. To get started, use the AWS Backup console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or AWS SDKs. Assign your RDS DB instances to a backup plan and specify a logically air-gapped vault in the same AWS Region as the copy destination. Share the vault for recovery or restore testing with other accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM), or safeguard vault access during account compromise using Multi-party approval . Once shared, you can initiate direct restore jobs from that account. This support is available in most AWS Regions where both logically air-gapped vault and Amazon RDS are available. For more information and detailed regional availability, visit the AWS Backup documentation . To learn more about logically air-gapped vaults for RDS, read the launch blog and visit the feature documentation and pricing page .

items.title: AWS WAF advanced rate-based rules are now available in AWS GovCloud (US), Thailand, and Mexico
items.description: AWS WAF advanced rate-based rules are now available in the Asia Pacific (Thailand), Mexico (Central), AWS GovCloud (US-East), and AWS GovCloud (US-West) Regions. Customers in these Regions can now aggregate requests using custom keys and choose a 1 or 2 minute evaluation window in addition to the existing 5 and 10 minute options, the same capabilities already available in other AWS Regions. A rate-based rule counts requests and applies an action, such as Block or CAPTCHA, when the request rate exceeds a limit you set. Previously, rate-based rules in these Regions could aggregate requests only by IP address and used a 5 or 10 minute evaluation window. Now you can aggregate by request components such as HTTP headers, cookies, query strings, URI paths, HTTP methods, and label namespaces, and combine up to five of them into a composite key. For example, you can limit login attempts per IP address and User-Agent pair, or per session cookie, which helps against attacks spread across many IP addresses. A shorter evaluation window detects request floods sooner, and a longer window catches slower, sustained attacks. You can configure these options in the AWS WAF console, the AWS CLI and SDKs, and AWS CloudFormation. There is no additional charge for these capabilities, and standard AWS WAF pricing applies. Advanced rate-based rules are now available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS WAF is available and in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, see Using rate-based rule statements in the AWS WAF Developer Guide.

items.title: AWS announces Networking Flexible Cost Allocation for Amazon VPC
items.description: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) now supports Networking Flexible Cost Allocation (FCA), which splits shared networking costs by the resources that actually drive them, so you can see what each team or application used. Until now, AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR), including CUR 2.0 in AWS Data Exports, showed networking usage as a single item, and most customers split it across teams with custom scripts and manual estimates. FCA splits this line item by the resources that generated it. It supports NAT gateway data processing and data transfer, including traffic to the internet, and in-Region Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) and VPC peering data transfer. Today, when several teams share a resource such as a NAT gateway, the account that owns it pays the full cost and can't see which team or application drove it. To work around this, some customers built custom scripts to analyze VPC Flow Logs, which takes ongoing engineering effort. Others used fixed-percentage splits, which overcharge some teams and undercharge others. FCA breaks down usage based on traffic sources, helping you accurately track financial metrics based on applications and teams. To get started, attach a cost allocation policy to a NAT gateway, VPC peering connection, or Amazon EC2 instance, then select Networking flexible cost allocation under split cost allocation data in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console. Allocated line items appear in your CUR within 24 hours. FCA changes only how costs are shown in your reports. Your bill and total charges stay the same. FCA is available at no additional charge. It's supported in all AWS commercial Regions except Middle East (Bahrain) and Middle East (UAE). It's also available in the China Regions. It is not available in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, visit the Networking FCA product page .

items.title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports ForceAuthn in SAML requests
items.description: AWS IAM Identity Center now gives you the option to require workforce users to re-authenticate with your external identity provider (IdP) each time their user interactive session expires. By default, when a user's session expires, IAM Identity Center renews it through the user's existing IdP session, and the user isn't prompted to sign in again. For organizations with strict security or compliance requirements that mandate explicit user verification at regular intervals, this automatic renewal may not meet policy requirements. When you set user re-authentication to Required and a user's user interactive session expires, IAM Identity Center prompts the user to re-authenticate with your external IdP. This helps you enforce stronger sign-in controls for regulated workloads. IAM Identity Center implements this by adding the SAML 2.0 ForceAuthn attribute to the SAML request sent to your IdP. You can configure user re-authentication for any IAM Identity Center instance (organization or account) that's connected to an external IdP as its identity source. The setting applies only to service provider initiated sign-ins, where users sign in through your AWS access portal URL. Changes to the user re-authentication setting are logged in AWS CloudTrail, so you can audit when it was turned on or off. User re-authentication is available in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available at no additional cost. To learn more, see Require user re-authentication in the AWS IAM Identity Center User Guide.

items.title: AWS Security Hub Network Scanning now supports scanning Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) database instances
items.description: AWS Security Hub Network Scanning now scans Amazon RDS DB instances to identify those that are reachable from the internet. Network Scanning automatically discovers existing and new RDS DB instances in your accounts and scans each instance that has Public Access configured. For each reachable port associated with a DB instance, Security Hub creates a finding with details about the instance and the reachable port. RDS scanning gives you more visibility into which resources in your environment are reachable from the internet. You can then investigate and update their access settings as needed. RDS scanning is turned on automatically for all customers who already have Network Scanning enabled. Network Scanning probes your resources from the internet to detect reachability, beyond what security group rules and route tables suggest. Security Hub Exposures then correlates these findings with other findings and resource configurations to assess broader risk. Existing Security Hub customers can enable Network Scanning in individual accounts and Regions, or across an organization with a configuration policy. For new Security Hub customers, Network Scanning is on by default. Network Scanning is included with Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost in all AWS commercial and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions that support Security Hub. To learn more, see the AWS Security Hub User Guide and the AWS Security Hub product page . For the full list of Regions, see the AWS Regional Services List .

items.title: AgentCore runtime instances are now available in six more AWS Regions
items.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances are now available in six additional AWS Regions: US West (N. California), Canada (Central), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), Europe (Stockholm), and Asia Pacific (Seoul). Runtime instances run your agents on Amazon EC2 instances while AgentCore handles provisioning, patching, scaling, and lifecycle management. By expanding to these AWS Regions, more teams can use runtime instance capabilities such as GPU-accelerated, memory-optimized, or compute-optimized instance types, and long-running agent sessions of up to 14 days. You can run your agents closer to your users to reduce invocation latency, and keep agent instances, storage volumes, and session data in the Region that your data residency requirements call for. With this expansion, you can use runtime instances in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo). You are charged for managing the provisioned compute, in addition to your Amazon EC2 costs. To get started, see the following resources: Supported AWS Regions in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide AgentCore pricing Runtime instances and capacity providers in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide

items.title: Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration now supported in CloudFormation
items.description: Aurora PostgreSQL now supports express configuration in AWS CloudFormation for infrastructure as code deployment. This launch enables you to automate the infrastructure deployment of your Aurora clusters through CloudFormation templates while benefiting from the speed of express configuration. Aurora PostgreSQL clusters created with express configuration allow you to create and query an Aurora serverless database in seconds. The new withExpressConfiguration createOnly property on the AWS::RDS::DBCluster resource creates both the cluster and its primary database instance from one property declaration. You don't need to model or manage the instance separately in your CloudFormation template. This simplifies your templates and makes it easier to manage Aurora clusters with express configuration through infrastructure as code. The CloudFormation support is available in all AWS Regions where Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration is offered. To learn more, see the Aurora User Guide and the AWS::RDS::DBCluster resource reference in the AWS CloudFormation documentation .

items.title: Grok 4.7 now available on Kiro in AWS GovCloud (US)
items.description: A new model is now available in the Kiro IDE and CLI for the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. Grok 4.7 is SpaceXSI's most capable model for coding and knowledge work. It's built to stay focused through hard tasks that run for hours, and it checks its work before moving on. Compared with Grok 4.6, it plans and recovers from errors more reliably in repo-scale coding work. Grok 4.7 is available with experimental support and a 500K context window. Requests up to 200K tokens use a 2.7x credit multiplier, and requests over 200K tokens are billed at 5.4x. Kiro administrators control which models are available to their users, so organizations can align model access with their internal policies. Ensure your IDE or CLI is updated to the latest version, then restart it to access the new model from the model selector. For more details, visit the GovCloud documentation , the monitoring and tracking guide , or contact your AWS account team. To learn more about Kiro, visit the Kiro product page .

items.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle reduces downtime for automatic minor version upgrades and scheduled maintenance
items.description: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now reduces downtime for automatic minor version upgrades, as well as minor version upgrades and operating system updates scheduled for your maintenance window. Shorter maintenance makes it easier to stay current on the latest Oracle minor versions and operating system updates with less disruption to your applications. If you turned on automatic minor version upgrade, your DB instances benefit automatically. To apply these upgrades and updates, RDS has to set up new resources as part of the maintenance. Previously, RDS set up these resources after the maintenance started, which made your downtime longer. Now, RDS prepares them up to 30 minutes before your maintenance window, while your DB instance keeps serving your workload. When the maintenance window opens, your DB instance is offline for less time because resources required for the maintenance are already prepared. This applies to both Enterprise Edition and Standard Edition 2 DB instances. The preparation never blocks or delays your own operations, and your DB instance stays available while RDS prepares. If a change that you make conflicts with the preparation, RDS rolls back the staged resources, and your change goes ahead. If the preparation can't finish, RDS still applies the maintenance in your window, without the preparation. New RDS events tell you when the preparation starts, when it finishes, and when it can't finish. RDS for Oracle will continue to introduce improvements that further reduce maintenance downtime. This capability is available at no additional cost in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where Amazon RDS for Oracle is available. To learn more, see Maintenance preparation , Amazon RDS event categories and event messages , and Maintaining a DB instance in the Amazon RDS User Guide.

items.title: AWS Security Hub CSPM now supports centralized configuration with AWS Organizations declarative policies
items.description: AWS Security Hub CSPM now supports AWS Organizations declarative policies. You can use them to enable Security Hub CSPM across all accounts and Regions in your organization and to define which security standards and controls are enabled. Policies can apply broadly to every account and Region, or target specific account and Region combinations. Declarative policies help keep each account's configuration aligned with its attached policy, which helps prevent configuration drift. You can also apply them automatically to new accounts, so each account starts with a baseline configuration as soon as it's created. Declarative policies are now the recommended way to manage Security Hub CSPM across an organization. They align with how other security services, such as Amazon GuardDuty, Amazon Inspector, and AWS Security Hub allow customers to manage configuration of the service. They also provide more flexibility, such as configuring Region-specific settings. You can continue to use central configuration until you're ready to migrate. When you are, use the migration process in the Security Hub CSPM console. It converts your existing central configuration policies into declarative policies and applies them to the appropriate accounts and regions. Declarative policies for Security Hub CSPM are available in all commercial, AWS GovCloud (US), and China Regions. To get started, see Migrating central configuration policies . To learn more, see Declarative policies in the AWS Security Hub CSPM User Guide and Security Hub CSPM policies in the AWS Organizations User Guide. To receive notifications about new Security Hub CSPM features and controls, subscribe to the Security Hub SNS topic . You can also try Security Hub CSPM at no cost for 30 days with the AWS Free Tier offering.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports OAuth 2.0 discovery URLs
items.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports OAuth 2.0 authorization server discovery URLs for both inbound JWT authorization and outbound OAuth credential providers. This update enables developers to configure AgentCore with OAuth 2.0 authorization servers that do not use OpenID Connect (OIDC). Previously, AgentCore Identity accepted only OIDC discovery URLs. Authorization servers that implement OAuth 2.0 without OIDC publish their metadata at a different well-known path and could not be used with AgentCore. With this launch, you can use either OIDC or OAuth 2.0 authorization server discovery URLs when you configure a JWT authorizer or a custom OAuth credential provider on AgentCore. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is available, at no additional cost. To learn more, see Configure inbound JWT authorizer and Add OAuth client using custom provider in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide .

items.title: AWS Secrets Manager now supports cross-account replication
items.description: AWS Secrets Manager now supports cross-account replication, enabling you to maintain a synchronized copy of a primary secret in a secondary AWS account for cross-account access, backup, and disaster recovery. Cross-account replication extends the existing multi-Region replication capability across account boundaries. With cross-account replication, platform or security teams can own and rotate a secret centrally, and each consuming account gets a local, always-current copy without any shared KMS keys or cross-account secret policies. The replica secret is a full, independent resource, encrypted with a customer managed KMS key owned by the replica account. Secrets Manager updates it automatically whenever the primary secret's value changes, including rotations. You can keep a live copy of critical secrets in a dedicated recovery or failover account, isolated from ransomware or a compromised primary account. If needed, the replica can be promoted to a standalone secret. Cross-account replication is available in all AWS Regions where Secrets Manager is available. For a list of regions where Secrets Manager is available, see the AWS Region table . To learn more, see Replicate secrets across AWS accounts in the Secrets Manager User Guide and the AssociateCrossAccountReplica API reference . For pricing details, see AWS Secrets Manager pricing .

items.title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports layout customization for designations
items.description: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports layout customization, a new capability that gives domain administrators control over which tools and left navigation items project members see based on their designation. Organizations with data engineering, analytics, and machine learning teams on a single platform can configure a layout within each designation definition, and that layout applies across every project in the domain without per-project configuration. Previously, all project members saw the same interface regardless of their role, creating confusion and potential governance issues. With layout customization, administrators define a layout as part of a designation that specifies which left navigation items are visible for project members assigned to that designation. When a project member opens a project, SageMaker Unified Studio resolves the member's designation and renders only the tools included in their designation's layout. For example, a SQL analyst designation can be configured to show only the Query Editor, while an ML engineer designation shows notebooks, training jobs, and model endpoints. Navigation items are configurable across categories including Data Analytics, artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML), Generative AI, and IDEs. If a project member navigates directly to a hidden page, they see an access-denied page. For members with multiple designations, visible tools are the union of all their designations' layouts. New navigation items added to SageMaker Unified Studio remain hidden for designations with a configured layout until an administrator adds them. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is available. To learn more, visit the Designations documentation.

items.title: AWS Batch on Amazon EKS adds Linux capabilities, seccomp, and pod-level settings
items.description: AWS Batch now supports additional Kubernetes security context settings in Amazon EKS job definitions, including Linux capabilities, seccomp profiles, and pod-level settings. For EKS clusters that enforce the Kubernetes Pod Security Standards restricted profile, you can now run AWS Batch jobs with only the privileges and system calls they require. To get started, use the RegisterJobDefinition API to set capabilities and seccompProfile in a container's securityContext , or set securityContext in podProperties to define pod-wide settings such as fsGroup . Container-level settings override pod-level defaults. You can configure these settings through the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or AWS CloudFormation. The additional security context settings for AWS Batch on Amazon EKS are now supported in all AWS Regions where AWS Batch is available. For more information, see the Amazon EKS properties section in the AWS Batch User Guide .

items.title: AWS Marketplace now supports VAT credit notes for deemed supply refunds
items.description: AWS Marketplace sellers can now submit Value Added Tax (VAT) credit notes for refunded deemed supply transactions through a self-service experience in AWS Partner Central. Previously, VAT was disbursed to sellers for eligible transactions, and when a buyer was later refunded, sellers had to contact AWS to submit the corresponding credit note. This launch simplifies post-refund VAT documentation for sellers. Sellers can view eligible refund line items in the VAT on deemed supply section, select the refunds covered by a credit note, upload a PDF or the applicable electronic invoice format, and track the submission status. Sellers can consolidate multiple eligible refunds into a single credit note where applicable and review the associated financial adjustment in the Seller Insights reporting. These capabilities are available for eligible AWS Marketplace transactions, including Channel Partner Private Offer (CPPO) transactions, in supported EU member states, Norway, and the United Kingdom. Country-specific invoicing and electronic-invoicing requirements continue to apply. To get started, sign in to AWS Partner Central and go to Settings → Tax information → VAT on deemed supply. To learn more, visit the AWS Marketplace Seller Guide or Deemed Supply FAQs .

items.title: AWS Systems Manager simplifies onboarding of Google Cloud VMs for centralized management
items.description: AWS Systems Manager Cloud Connector now extends simplified multicloud onboarding support to Google Cloud, making it easy to connect your existing Google Cloud VMs to Systems Manager for centralized management alongside AWS, on-premises, and Azure resources without manual agent installation. Previously, managing virtual machines across multiple cloud providers often required coordinating and setting up configurations separately in each environment. With Cloud Connector for Google Cloud, you can automatically deploy the SSM Agent to Google Cloud VMs at scale. Once connected, Google Cloud VMs appear alongside EC2 instances, on-premises servers, and other multicloud resources in a unified view, enabling you to use Session Manager, Automation runbooks, Run Command, State Manager, Patch Manager, and Inventory across AWS, on-premises, Azure, and Google Cloud from a single workflow. This simplifies operations for teams managing infrastructure across multiple clouds, enabling them to standardize management practices and reduce operational complexity. Cloud Connector for Google Cloud is available in Africa (Cape Town), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong, Hyderabad, Jakarta, Malaysia, Melbourne, Mumbai, New Zealand, Osaka, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Taipei, Thailand, Tokyo), Canada (Central, Calgary), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Milan, Paris, Spain, Stockholm, Zurich), Israel (Tel Aviv), Mexico (Central), South America (Sao Paulo), US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), and US West (N. California, Oregon). To learn more, visit the AWS Systems Manager documentation.

items.title: Amazon Cognito now supports OAuth 2.0 token exchange
items.description: Amazon Cognito now supports OAuth 2.0 token exchange (RFC 8693). Amazon Cognito helps you add sign-up, sign-in, and access control to your web applications, mobile applications, and AI agents. With token exchange, a service or AI agent acting on a user's behalf can exchange the user's token for a new token scoped to a specific downstream service. Previously, a service that called another service on a user's behalf had to forward the user's original token or build and maintain its own token minting logic. With token exchange, you can issue a new token that has a narrower scope than the original token, is bound to a single audience, and comes without a refresh token. When you include an actor token, Cognito adds an act claim that identifies the intermediary, so downstream services can tell a request that an agent made on a user's behalf from one the user made directly. For example, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server can exchange a user's token for a narrowly scoped token to call a backend API, with the act claim recording the MCP server as the actor. You can exchange tokens through the token endpoint or with the new GetDerivedToken API . Token exchange is available on the Essentials and Plus feature plans in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available. To learn more, see exchanging tokens for downstream services in the Amazon Cognito Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon Aurora and RDS now support Graviton5-based R9g database instances
items.description: AWS Graviton5-based R9g database instances are now generally available for Amazon Aurora with PostgreSQL compatibility and MySQL compatibility, and for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB.   Graviton5-based R9g instances provide up to a 30% performance improvement and up to a 22% price-performance improvement for on-demand pricing over Graviton4-based instances of equivalent sizes on Amazon Aurora, depending on database engine, version, and workload. Built on the AWS Nitro System, R9g instances are available in nine sizes, from large to 48xlarge. They deliver up to 192 vCPUs, an 8:1 ratio of memory to vCPU, up to 100 Gbps of networking bandwidth, and up to 72 Gbps of bandwidth to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS).  You can get started using the R9g database instances through the Amazon RDS Management Console or by using the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI). The instances are available in US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), and Europe (Frankfurt) regions. For the specific engine versions that support these instance classes, see the Aurora and RDS documentation. For pricing, see Amazon Aurora pricing and Amazon RDS pricing .

items.title: Amazon MWAA now supports fine-grained access control with IAM Identity Center and multi-team environments
items.description: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA) now supports fine-grained access control, giving administrators precise control over who can access which workflows and resources in an Apache Airflow environment. Fine-grained access control is delivered through two new capabilities: IAM Identity Center integration and multi-team environments. With IAM Identity Center integration, users sign in to the Apache Airflow UI with their corporate identity provider. Authorization is evaluated per request using IAM policies attached to IAM Identity Center Permission Sets, with condition keys that scope access by resource type (DAGs, connections, variables, pools, and more), action, and specific resource ID. With multi-team environments, several teams can share a single MWAA environment. Each team gets its own DAG folder in Amazon S3, and users see only shared DAGs plus their own teams' DAGs based on IAM Identity Center group membership. Teams reduce cost through shared infrastructure and simplify management by configuring environment settings once. Multi-team environments are based on the Apache Airflow multi-team feature, which is currently in preview. These features are available in all AWS Regions where Amazon MWAA is available. To learn more, visit the IAM Identity Center integration documentation and the multi-team environments documentation .

items.title: Apache Airflow UI available in Amazon MWAA Serverless
items.description: Amazon MWAA Serverless provides the native Apache Airflow UI for your workflows. You can browse workflows, inspect workflow runs and task instances, read task logs, view a workflow's source and versions, and start a workflow run. The UI uses the permissions of the IAM identity that opens it and shows only what that identity can read, so read-only access is possible. AWS CloudTrail records the calls the UI makes under your identity. You can open the Airflow UI from the Amazon MWAA console, the AWS CLI, or the API. Teams already familiar with Airflow can use the interface they know to work with their workflows. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon MWAA Serverless is available. For more information, see the AWS Region table . To get started, see Access the Airflow UI . Apache Airflow is a trademark of the Apache Software Foundation .

items.title: Amazon Connect Customer supports merging and linking related cases in the agent workspace
items.description: Amazon Connect Customer now lets agents merge and link related cases in the agent workspace, so they can resolve customer issues faster and respond consistently. When a customer contacts a business about the same issue more than once, or on different channels, the history can end up split across several cases. Agents can merge those cases into one case with a single, consolidated history. For example, an agent can merge the chat and email cases a customer opened about a delayed shipment. Agents can also link related cases, such as cases from different customers affected by the same issue, so they can coordinate one consistent response for every affected customer. Cases is available in the following AWS regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .

items.title: Amazon SNS now supports push notifications in four additional AWS Regions
items.description: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) now supports sending push notifications in the Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Europe (Zurich), and AWS GovCloud (US-East) Regions. Amazon SNS is a fully managed pub/sub service that provides message delivery to multiple endpoints, including AWS Lambda, Amazon SQS, Amazon Data Firehose, HTTP, SMS (via AWS End User Messaging), push notifications, and email. With this launch, customers in these four additional Regions can use Amazon SNS to send push notifications to the following supported push notification services: Amazon Device Messaging (ADM), Apple Push Notification Service (APNs), Baidu Cloud Push (Baidu), Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM), and Windows Push Notification Services (WNS). For the full list of Regions from which you can send push notifications, see Supported Regions and Countries in the Amazon SNS Developer Guide. For more information, see the Amazon SNS push notifications documentation .

items.title: AWS Quick enhances granular governance with the ability to restrict structured data sources
items.description: Today, AWS Quick is announcing the general availability of structured data connector restrictions through custom permissions. This capability gives administrators granular control over which types of data sources users can create, update, or share, helping organizations enforce data governance requirements while enabling self-service analytics. With this feature, administrators can configure custom permissions profiles in Enterprise edition through the Quick UI, APIs, or AWS Command Line Interface. For example, an organization can allow users to create Amazon Redshift data sources while restricting the creation of file-upload data sources. Administrators can also prevent users from sharing data sources for a particular connector. Create, update, and share restrictions can be configured independently, providing more precise controls than restrictions that apply to all data source types. This feature is now available in all supported AWS Quick Regions listed here . To learn more, check our documentation here .

items.title: Amazon Route 53 Domains now supports self-service restore for expired and deleted domains
items.description: Amazon Route 53 Domains now lets you restore an expired or recently deleted domain yourself, using the Amazon Route 53 console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. Previously, restoring a domain required a request to AWS Support. Now you can recover a domain lost to a missed renewal, an expired payment method, or an accidental deletion, and restore the website, email, and applications that depend on it. To restore a domain, you enter the domain name, review the restoration price, accept the charge, and submit the request. Route 53 works with the top-level domain (TLD) registry to reactivate the registration and return the domain to your AWS account. Most TLD registries support restoration, and each registry sets how long after expiration or deletion a domain can still be restored. Restoring a domain typically costs more than registering or renewing one. To learn more, see Restoring an expired or deleted domain in the Route 53 Developer Guide, or visit the Amazon Route 53 Domains page . For a complete list of supported TLDs, see the Route 53 TLD list . For pricing, visit the Route 53 pricing page .

items.title: EC2 Image Builder console now integrates with the DevOps Agent for troubleshooting and resource creation
items.description: EC2 Image Builder now integrates with the AWS DevOps Agent directly in the Image Builder console, enabling you to troubleshoot failed image pipelines and create resources directly from the console chat panel. You can diagnose up to 50 failed pipelines at once and ask follow-up questions in the same conversation. You can also choose to create resources by describing what you want, and the agent populates the console with values the service has already validated. With this integration, diagnosing a failed pipeline no longer requires manually inspecting build logs, cross-referencing error codes, or iterating through configuration fixes, saving you significant time and expertise. The agent reads build logs, workflow steps, components, and network configuration, then provides the root cause and the steps to fix it. For resource creation,  the agent verifies the configuration before populating the console for you to review and submit. If you troubleshoot or build with your own AI agents, the new EC2 Image Builder skill in the AWS Agent Toolkit provides you the same troubleshooting and creation capabilities. This feature is available in all commercial regions. To get started, open the EC2 Image Builder console and use the DevOps Agent from the console panel. For more information, see the EC2 Image Builder documentation and for pricing refer DevOps agent Pricing page .

items.title: AWS Glue announces automatic version upgrades for Apache Spark jobs
items.description: AWS Glue introduces automatic version upgrades, a capability that keeps your Apache Spark jobs current on the latest AWS Glue runtime without manual coordination. Staying current on supported runtimes gives your jobs the latest security patches, performance improvements, and support for evolving table formats such as Apache Iceberg. Auto upgrades include multiple levels of validations including assessing jobs for compatibility with the upgraded runtime, obtaining your consent before executing jobs on a newer version, and validating upgraded job runs against each job's established output profile, so your jobs upgrade with the right guardrails in place. By setting a job's version to "Auto", upgrades that once required weeks of planning and execution now happen automatically. Platform teams can standardize runtime versions across large fleets without chasing individual job owners, and business units without a central upgrade team can keep their jobs current hands-free. Each job is validated against its established output schema, data volume, latency, and format before it upgrades, so you can advance with confidence. Jobs that need code changes keep running safely on their current version, and AWS Glue provides an upgrade analysis with specific fixes you can apply directly or with the Apache Spark upgrade agent. Auto upgrades for AWS Glue are available in all AWS Commercial Regions. To get started, select "Auto" as the AWS Glue version when creating or updating an Apache Spark job using the AWS Glue Studio or AWS CLI, API, and SDKs. Alternatively, you can update multiple jobs at once using the AWS Glue skill to manage your jobs . To learn more, visit the AWS Glue documentation .

items.title: AWS Backup adds logically air-gapped vault support for Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive
items.description: AWS Backup logically air-gapped vault now supports Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive. Logically air-gapped vaults are a type of AWS Backup vault that allows secure sharing of backups across accounts and AWS Organizations, supporting direct restore to reduce recovery time from a data loss event. You can now archive Amazon EBS backups held in a logically air-gapped vault to Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive, a low-cost tier for snapshots you rarely access. A logically air-gapped vault stores immutable backups that are locked by default, and isolated with encryption using AWS owned keys or customer-managed keys. This helps you meet long-term retention and compliance requirements at lower storage cost. You can get started using the AWS Backup console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or AWS SDKs. In a backup plan rule that runs monthly or less often, specify a logically air-gapped vault as the primary backup destination or copy destination. Then enable Archive Amazon EBS snapshots in the backup rule lifecycle or copy lifecycle and set the time in warm storage before the backup transitions. This support is available in all AWS Regions where both logically air-gapped vault and Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive are available. For more information and detailed regional availability, visit the AWS Backup documentation . To learn more about logically air-gapped vaults, visit the product documentation and pricing page .

items.title: Amazon FSx for Lustre now offers a 75% lower minimum throughput capacity and metadata IOPS for Intelligent-Tiering file systems
items.description: Amazon FSx for Lustre is reducing the minimum provisioned throughput capacity and metadata IOPS on Intelligent-Tiering file systems by 75%, allowing you to use Intelligent-Tiering even more cost-effectively for high-performance computing (HPC) and machine learning workloads that start with small datasets and grow over time. The FSx for Lustre Intelligent-Tiering storage class delivers the lowest-cost and only fully elastic Lustre file storage in the cloud. It is optimized for workloads that mix hot and cold data and do not require consistent SSD-level performance. A file system's throughput capacity determines the read and write speeds supported by its underlying file servers, and its level of metadata IOPS determines how many files and directories you can create, read, and delete per second. Today’s launch reduces the minimum throughput capacity on an Intelligent-Tiering file system from 4,000 to 1,000 MBps and the minimum metadata performance from 6,000 to 1,500 IOPS.  The lower throughput capacity and metadata IOPS levels are available on new FSx for Lustre Intelligent-Tiering file systems in all AWS Regions where the Intelligent-Tiering storage class is available. To learn more, see Performance characteristics of Intelligent-Tiering storage class in the Amazon FSx for Lustre User Guide.

items.title: Amazon Route 53 now supports record set protection
items.description: Amazon Route 53 now supports record set protection, which helps DNS administrators prevent accidental changes to critical DNS records in their hosted zones. This feature allows you to protect records such as those at the zone apex, MX records, and production endpoints directly in the hosted zone. Any change to a protected record is blocked until the protection is removed by an authorized user. Previously, to lock specific records, you had to write record-level conditions into the IAM policies of every user and role that could change your hosted zones. When those policies blocked a change, the caller had no indication of whether the record was protected or why. Now you can protect records by name and type directly in the hosted zone. A single protection covers all records with that name and type, including records with different set identifiers; weighted, latency, and other routing policy records are protected together. You can also create a protection proactively before the record exists, preventing records from being created for that name and type. Each protection can include an optional comment of up to 256 characters, allowing you to indicate the reason for the protection. You can manage protections using the Route 53 console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs through the CreateResourceRecordSetProtections, DeleteResourceRecordSetProtections, and ListResourceRecordSetProtections API actions. To control who can remove protections, restrict the DeleteResourceRecordSetProtections permission in IAM policies. Record set protection is available in all AWS commercial Regions where public and private hosted zones are available today. To learn more, see Protecting records from changes in the Amazon Route 53 Developer Guide.

items.title: Amazon RDS for SQL Server now supports M8id and R8id instances
items.description: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports M8id and R8id instances. These instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors, available only on AWS, and include local NVMe SSD storage. They scale up to 384 vCPUs, 3 TiB of memory, and 22.8 TB of local NVMe SSD storage. That's 4x the vCPUs and memory and more than 6x the local storage of M5d and R5d instances. When you create or modify a DB instance to use M8id or R8id, RDS for SQL Server automatically places the tempdb data and log files on the local NVMe instance store. This gives tempdb lower read and write latency than Amazon EBS storage. Your database data and log files stay on Amazon EBS. Because snapshots don't include tempdb files on the instance store, your snapshots are smaller and use less of your free backup storage. To learn more, see Instance store support for the tempdb database on Amazon RDS for SQL Server . To use the new M8id and R8id instances, you can modify your existing RDS database instance or create a new RDS database instance from the RDS Management Console, or using the AWS SDK or CLI. M8id and R8id instances are available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Stockholm), Europe (Spain), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and Asia Pacific (Malaysia). For pricing details, see Amazon RDS for SQL Server Pricing .

items.title: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink introduces enhanced snapshots
items.description: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink now supports enhanced snapshots, a capability that lets you capture, export, and restore application state across Apache Flink applications and AWS Regions, so you can run blue/green deployments, easily migrate self-managed workloads to Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink without losing state, and keep backup in a secondary Region for cross-Region recovery. To deploy an application update without pausing processing for blue/green deployments, create an enhanced snapshot from an application and use it to start a second application. To migrate a self-managed workload, import its Apache Flink savepoint into Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink as an enhanced snapshot. For cross-Region recovery, export an enhanced snapshot to an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket, and replicate the exported state to a bucket in a secondary Region. Enhanced snapshots are available today for applications on Apache Flink 1.20 and later in all AWS Regions where Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink is available except European Sovereign Cloud (Germany). You pay for enhanced snapshot storage per GB-month as durable application backups. To learn more and get started, see enhanced snapshots in the Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink Developer Guide. You can also use Agent Toolkit for AWS with Kiro, Claude Code, or Cursor for guidance on building and operating Flink applications with enhanced snapshots.

items.title: AWS Backup now supports resource modifiers for Amazon EKS restores
items.description: Today, AWS Backup announces support for resource modifiers when restoring Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) backups. Resource modifiers let you transform Kubernetes resources during a restore, so you can adapt a restored cluster to its target environment. When you restore an EKS backup that has been copied across accounts or across AWS Regions, the restored cluster can carry references tied to the source environment, such as IAM roles, database endpoints, and Amazon ECR registry URIs. Previously, you had to locate and update these references manually after every restore, which was time consuming and error prone. With resource modifiers, you can define transformation rules once via a YAML file, and AWS Backup applies them automatically as part of the restore, improving the reliability of your cross-account and cross-Region disaster recovery workflows. AWS Backup support for resource modifiers for Amazon EKS backups is available in all commercial AWS Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To get started, see the AWS Backup Documentation and read the launch blog .
